headline: The investment bank Barclays downgraded Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and NetApp, and their shares fell sharply because it sees no clear sign yet of lasting AI spending growth.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; it is one bank's view.
importance_line: Shareholders and pension funds that hold these server and storage makers lost most on the day; the doubt is that this is one bank's opinion, and the three stocks are still far above where they began the year.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Barclays cut its ratings on Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and NetApp to 'equal weight' (a neutral view) from 'overweight' on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, saying it does not see 'a meaningful AI inflection yet', and the shares fell 11%, 8% and 7%. Barclays said higher prices caused by a shortage of memory parts have propped up revenue, so sales growth could slow once those prices normalise.
